categories.name: Operation
categories.description: Choose one main operation. Operands name disk files, archive members or input archives according to the operation.

options.summary: Create a new archive
options.detail: Also spelled -c. An existing archive at the output path is replaced. Named directories are archived recursively by default. In traditional syntax, tar cfv out.tar src takes option values in letter order. In a dashed cluster the value-taking letter goes last, as in tar -cvf out.tar src.

options.summary: Extract files from an archive
options.detail: Also spelled -x, --get. With no member names, extract all members. To select files, use their stored names. Extraction writes under the current directory by default and can replace existing files. Later copies of the same member normally overwrite earlier copies.

options.summary: List archive contents
options.detail: Also spelled -t. Supply stored member names to limit the listing. Add -v to see sizes, permissions and modification times.

options.summary: Compare archive members with filesystem files
options.detail: Also spelled -d, --compare. Checks contents and metadata against files with the same names on disk. Extra files on disk are ignored. Exit status 1 indicates differences.

options.summary: Add files to the end of an archive
options.detail: Also spelled -r. Name files on disk. A repeated name adds another member and keeps the earlier copy. Updating an archive in place requires uncompressed output.

options.summary: Append new files and newer versions
options.detail: Also spelled -u. Name files on disk. Tar compares modification times with archived copies and leaves earlier members in place. Compressed archives cannot be updated in place.

options.summary: Append whole archives to another archive
options.detail: Also spelled -A, --concatenate. Give the destination with -f and existing uncompressed archives as operands. Tar does not validate their formats. Appending several inputs at once can leave internal end markers. Use -i when reading past them or append one archive per invocation.

options.summary: Remove named members from an archive
options.detail: Supply stored member names. By default tar removes every matching occurrence. Use an uncompressed archive on rewritable media.

options.summary: Print or test the archive volume label
options.detail: With no operands tar prints the label if present. Supply label patterns as separate operands for a silent test. Status 0 means a match and 1 means no match.

options.summary: Select legacy format or ownership behavior
options.detail: With --create, -o writes V7 format. With --extract, -o restores files as the extracting user. An archive filename belongs to -f.

options.summary: Compress or decompress with gzip
options.detail: Also spelled -z, --gunzip, --ungzip. When reading a regular archive file, tar normally detects gzip automatically. Specify the method for compressed input from a pipe or non-seekable tape.

options.detail: Also spelled -J. When reading a regular archive file, tar normally detects xz automatically. Specify the method for compressed input from a pipe or non-seekable tape.

options.detail: Also spelled -Z, --uncompress. Select the filter explicitly for compressed input from a pipe. Reading an ordinary archive file normally detects compression.

options.summary: Compress or decompress with lzip
options.detail: Use the filter explicitly for lzip input on a pipe or non-seekable tape.

options.summary: Use the configured LZMA compression program

options.summary: Compress or decompress with lzop

options.summary: Compress or decompress with Zstandard

options.summary: Choose compression from the output archive suffix
options.detail: Also spelled -a. During creation a recognized name such as .tar.gz selects its filter. A pipe has no filename suffix. Reading regular archives normally detects compression without -a.

options.summary: Disable suffix-based compression selection
